Read docs/TASK_ccledger.md FIRST (it is in your context): section 2.1 defines the INPUT (a Claude Code session log), section 2.2 the OUTPUT shape `Api Call`, section 2.3 the exact names. Do not guess names or keys -- every one you need is there. contour.yaml's Function `Load Session` is the behaviour in prose.

Write TWO new files.

1. `ccledger/load.py` -- module-level names, exactly these: `SYNTHETIC = "<synthetic>"` and `def load_session(path) -> List[dict]`.

`path` is a `.jsonl` file. Subagent logs live in `<path without .jsonl>/subagents/*.jsonl` (sorted by name); the directory may be absent. Read the main file first, then each subagent file. For every line: `json.loads`, and on `ValueError` skip the line. Keep only records with `type == "assistant"`, a dict `message` with a non-empty `usage`, and `message.model != SYNTHETIC`. A streamed answer produces SEVERAL records with the same `message.id`: collapse them into ONE call keyed by `message.id` (fall back to the record's `requestId`, then `uuid`, when `message.id` is missing) -- `usage` is taken from the LAST record seen, `tools` accumulate `tool_use` blocks from `message.content` in order of appearance, `timestamp` and `model` and `stop_reason` come from the first record that has them (stop_reason may be updated by a later record if the first is None). Keep first-appearance order (OrderedDict / dict insertion order); main-file calls come before subagent calls.

Each returned call is the dict of section 2.2 `Api Call`: `{"id", "model", "source", "timestamp", "stop_reason", "usage": {"input", "output", "cache_read", "cache_write_1h", "cache_write_5m"}, "tools": [{"name", "input"}]}`. `source` is `"main"` for the main file and `"subagent:<basename of the file>"` for a subagent file. usage mapping: `input` <- `input_tokens`, `output` <- `output_tokens`, `cache_read` <- `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_write_1h` <- `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`, `cache_write_5m` <- `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`; when the `cache_creation` block is absent, the whole `cache_creation_input_tokens` goes to `cache_write_1h`. Every missing field is 0; a non-int value is 0. `input` of a tool block is `block.get("input") or {}`; `name` is `block.get("name")`.

A module docstring that says what the module does NOT do (no pricing, no classification, no printing, no network), comments that explain WHY (the streaming duplicates, the fallback key), Python 3.9-compatible syntax (typing.List/Dict/Optional; no `match`, no `X | Y`). Standard library only. This is the ONLY module of the project that opens files.

2. `tests/test_load.py` -- unittest, every assertion with a `msg=`. The fixture is `tests/fixtures/sessions/sample.jsonl` with `tests/fixtures/sessions/sample/subagents/agent-1.jsonl` and `agent-2.jsonl`; build the path with `os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "fixtures", "sessions", "sample.jsonl")`. The ground truth for that fixture is the table in TASK section 2.1 -- assert EXACTLY: 124 calls in total, 79 with `source == "main"`, 33 from `agent-1.jsonl` and 12 from `agent-2.jsonl`; the five token sums over ALL calls equal the right-hand column of the table (input 1794, output 145884, cache_read 13167719, cache_write_1h 235500, cache_write_5m 234921) and over main-only calls equal the left-hand column (1692, 92607, 10865143, 235500, 0); the number of `assistant` lines in the main file is 168 (so collapsing really happened); models are {"claude-fable-5-1": 79, "claude-opus-5-5": 45}; the ids are unique. Also synthetic cases written to a temp dir: a file with two records sharing one `message.id` where the second carries a different usage and a tool_use -> one call with the LAST usage and one tool; a `<synthetic>` record and a broken line -> both skipped; a record without `cache_creation` -> all of `cache_creation_input_tokens` in `cache_write_1h`; an empty file -> `[]`; a file with no subagents directory -> main calls only; a record with `type == "user"` -> ignored. Read the fixture excerpt `tests/fixtures/sessions/sample-excerpt.jsonl` in your context to see the real record shapes before writing the synthetic ones.

Read docs/TASK_ccledger.md (in your context): section 2.2 `Price Table` and `Api Call` (the `usage` dict this module receives), section 2.3 the exact names. Do not invent names.

Write TWO new files.

1. `ccledger/price.py` -- module-level names, exactly these:

    PRICE_TABLE = {"opus": {"in": 5.0, "out": 25.0, "cr": 0.5, "cw1h": 10.0, "cw5m": 6.25},
                   "sonnet": {"in": 3.0, "out": 15.0, "cr": 0.3, "cw1h": 6.0, "cw5m": 3.75},
                   "haiku": {"in": 1.0, "out": 5.0, "cr": 0.1, "cw1h": 2.0, "cw5m": 1.25}}
    def family(model) -> str
    def price_call(usage, model, table=PRICE_TABLE) -> float

Prices are US dollars per MILLION tokens. `family`: case-insensitive substring test on `model or ""` -- contains "haiku" -> "haiku", contains "sonnet" -> "sonnet", anything else (opus, fable, None, unknown) -> "opus". `price_call`: `usage` is the Api Call usage dict `{"input", "output", "cache_read", "cache_write_1h", "cache_write_5m"}`; result = (input*in + output*out + cache_read*cr + cache_write_1h*cw1h + cache_write_5m*cw5m) / 1_000_000. A missing key or a non-numeric value counts as 0; `usage` None -> 0.0. Pure: no I/O, no imports beyond typing. Module docstring says what the module does NOT do (no parsing, no summing across calls, no calibration) and WHY the table is data (prices change; calibration against cost-state is a later deck). Python 3.9 syntax.

2. `tests/test_price.py` -- unittest with `msg=` on every assertion: family for "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001" -> haiku, "claude-sonnet-5" -> sonnet, "claude-opus-5-5" -> opus, "claude-fable-5-1" -> opus, None -> opus, "HAIKU" -> haiku; a hand-computed example: usage {input 1000, output 2000, cache_read 1_000_000, cache_write_1h 100_000, cache_write_5m 0} on an opus model = 0.005 + 0.05 + 0.5 + 1.0 = 1.555 (assertAlmostEqual, places 9); the same usage on haiku = 0.001 + 0.01 + 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.311; empty dict -> 0.0; None -> 0.0; missing keys -> only the present ones count; a custom `table` argument is honoured; a non-numeric value ("x") counts as 0 without raising.

instruction:
Read docs/TASK_ccledger.md (in your context) section 2.3 for the exact names and contour.yaml's Function `Classify Call` for the rule. Do not invent names or categories.

Write TWO new files.

1. `ccledger/classify.py` -- module-level names, exactly these:

    CATEGORIES = ("write", "test", "git", "ops", "web", "agent", "read", "other", "talk")
    def bash_category(command) -> str
    def classify_call(tools) -> str

`tools` is the Api Call list `[{"name": str, "input": dict}]`. Category of one tool: Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit -> "write"; Bash -> `bash_category(input.get("command", ""))`; WebFetch/WebSearch -> "web"; Agent/Task/SendMessage -> "agent"; Read/Grep/Glob/LS -> "read"; any other name -> "other". `classify_call` returns the FIRST category of CATEGORIES (in that order, which is the priority) that any tool of the call maps to; an empty list -> "talk".

`bash_category(command)`: judge the command string case-insensitively by WHOLE WORDS (regex with `\\b`), in this priority: "write" when it contains a redirection `>` or `>>` (outside nothing -- a plain substring test for `>` is fine), or the words tee, `sed -i`, cp, mv, mkdir, touch, or the phrase `git commit`; "test" for pytest, unittest, vitest, `npm test`, `npm run test`, tsc, ruff, mypy; "git" for `git` followed by add/commit/push/checkout/merge/rebase/stash/pull/fetch/tag/reset; "ops" for ssh, scp, docker, kubectl, hcloud, gh, curl, wget; everything else -> "read". Note the priority means `git commit` is "write" (it changes the repository), `git push` is "git", `gitk` is not git (whole words), `pytest ... > log` is "write" because redirection wins. Pure module: no I/O; `re` and typing only; docstring names what it does NOT do (no pricing, no reading of files) and WHY the priority order is what it is (a call that both read and wrote is a writing call -- that is what the orientation metric counts). Python 3.9 syntax.

2. `tests/test_classify.py` -- unittest with `msg=` on every assertion: one example per category through `classify_call` (nine tests at least); priority: [Edit, Read] -> write, [Read, WebFetch] -> web, [Agent, Read] -> agent; Bash cases through both functions: "git commit -m x" -> write, "git push origin main" -> git, "gitk" -> read, "pytest -q --tb=short" -> test, "PYTEST -q" -> test (case), "ssh host ls" -> ops, "gh pr create" -> ops, "ls -la" -> read, "cat a.py > b.py" -> write, "echo x | tee f" -> write, "sed -n 1,5p f" -> read but "sed -i s/a/b/ f" -> write, "npm run test" -> test, "cp a b" -> write, an empty command -> read; `classify_call([])` -> talk; a tool with an unknown name -> other; a Bash tool with no `input` key -> read.

1. `ccledger/render.py` -- module-level names, exactly these: `MISSING = "\u2014"` (the em dash) and `def render_ledger(ledger) -> str` and `def render_table(ledgers) -> str`. Pure: dict in, string out; no I/O, no printing, no imports of other ccledger modules. Read every value with `.get` and print MISSING for None/absent.

`render_ledger(ledger)`: a heading `# Session <session_id>` then one line with span start, end and seconds; a Markdown table of tokens with rows input, output, cache_read, cache_write_1h, cache_write_5m and a final row `cache_read share of input` = cache_read / (input + cache_read + cache_write_1h + cache_write_5m) as a percent with one decimal (MISSING when the denominator is 0); one line `cost: estimated $X.XXXX, recorded $Y.YYYY, ratio Z.ZZ` (each MISSING when None); a table of categories in the order write, test, git, ops, web, agent, read, other, talk with columns calls, usd (4 decimals), share of calls (percent, one decimal); two lines `calls before first write: N` and `calls before first commit: N` (MISSING when None); a line `calls: total T, main M, subagents S`; a line of models `model: calls` comma-joined. The words `estimated`, `recorded`, `before first write`, `before first commit` MUST appear verbatim (the tests and the spec check them). Never include anything that is not a number, a model name, a tool name or the session id.

`render_table(ledgers)`: one Markdown table with header `session | calls | output | cache_read | usd | before first write | before first commit`, one row per ledger in the given order, then a final row `total` with the sums of calls, output, cache_read and usd (the two orientation columns show MISSING in the total row). Empty list -> the header and a total row of zeros.

Deterministic: same input, same string; no timestamps of "now". Python 3.9 syntax. Docstring says what the module does NOT do (no computing of numbers beyond the two shares, no reading, no writing).

2. `tests/test_render.py` -- unittest with `msg=`: build one full Ledger dict by hand with the exact keys of section 2.2 and small numbers (e.g. calls total 5, main 3, subagents 2; tokens input 100, output 200, cache_read 900, cache_write_1h 0, cache_write_5m 0; cost estimated 0.1234, recorded 0.1, ratio 1.234; orientation 2 and None) and assert: the heading contains the session id; the four mandatory phrases appear; `\u2014` appears exactly where the None values are (before first commit, and in a second ledger with cost recorded None); `cache_read share of input` row shows `90.0%`; all nine categories appear in order; `[text` does not appear anywhere even when the ledger's session_id is normal; an EMPTY dict `{}` renders without raising and contains the heading and every mandatory phrase with MISSING; two renders of the same ledger are equal; `render_table` of two ledgers has exactly 2 data rows plus a total row whose calls equals the sum; `render_table([])` has a header and a zero total row.
